solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Indicator of wind's blow

definitions.meaning: a windsock on an airfield shows which way the wind blows, often shortened to the single word
to hit someone hard, a punch

explanation.definitionFit: A windsock is often called just by its last syllable, and as a verb or noun the word also means a hard punch.

clue.text: Host a former athlete dispatched outside

indicators.note: one word stands outside the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to dispatch something is to send it, so sent
Steve Cram is a retired British middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A one-time sportsman is sent off from a party he was hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests a party giver, but it is the consecrated bread of the Eucharist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Host is the consecrated communion wafer, which is the sacred rite of the Eucharist itself.

clue.text: Provide comfort to computer games player

definitions.meaning: to soothe someone in their grief
a games machine such as a PlayStation or Xbox, used to play video games

explanation.definitionFit: To soothe in distress is this verb, and a video-gaming machine attached to a TV is this noun.

clue.text: Model problem

definitions.meaning: someone who sits or stands for an artist or photographer
a puzzling question or tricky conundrum

explanation.definitionFit: A sitter for a painter strikes poses, and a puzzling question is informally called a teaser of this kind.

clue.text: Fish expert catches indefinite number possibly

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, as a net catches fish

parts.note: an ace is an expert
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A skilled angler might land a large number of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning perhaps or maybe, implying something might happen.

clue.text: Regular correspondent's report of Scottish island

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the island's name is said out loud

parts.note: Staffa is a small Hebridean island, home of Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: A journalist files a story about a remote island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the island's name and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist on the permanent payroll of a newspaper, as opposed to a freelancer, is a regular writer there.

clue.text: One protected by terrible horn

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded by its guard, so one letter goes inside
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something is kept safe by a fearsome horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' jumbles HORN into RHNO, and 'protected by' puts I inside it; the whole clue describes the animal too.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African or Asian beast is armed with a formidable nose horn.

clue.text: Cut down garden weed

definitions.meaning: to shorten or reduce, as with wages or a tail
a broad-leaved weed of the genus Rumex, common in British gardens

explanation.definitionFit: To reduce pay or curtail a tail is this verb, and it is also the common name of a broad-leaved Rumex weed.

clue.text: Changes the character of area in false set

indicators.note: the letter for area is placed inside the word for false teeth

parts.note: dentures are a false set of teeth

explanation.surface: Someone changes the nature of an area within a fake film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false set' looks like an anagram signal on SET, but it means a set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter the essential nature of something, as alcohol is made undrinkable or proteins are altered by heat.

clue.text: It will make you go about carrying a sign of injury

indicators.note: one word carries others inside it

parts.note: CA is circa, about
a scar is the mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off bearing a wound mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like travel, but it means to empty the bowels: this is a bark used as a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascara is a purgative made from buckthorn bark, so it brings on a bowel movement.

clue.text: Protector of wildlife cites innovators in development

indicators.note: being developed means being reworked and changed, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ecologist quotes inventors who are working on new projects.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of CITES INNOVATORS are rearranged under the signal 'in development'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns to preserve the natural environment and its wild creatures from harm.

clue.text: Acknowledge version of the Bible with cry of pain

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone confesses their faith over a Bible while wincing in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for affirming or declaring something to be true, i.e. admitting or vouching for it.

clue.text: Presenter of TV show with unusual format introducing new name

indicators.note: the word format has a letter brought into it before the shuffle
an unusual version of something is altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television host fronts a programme with a quirky new format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts N (new) into FORMAT; 'unusual' shuffles those seven letters into FRONTMA, and a final N for name completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who fronts and hosts a television programme is its lead presenter.

clue.text: Observe large ship's make-up

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
a liner is a big passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone watches a big ocean vessel and notes its construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like the ship's composition, but it means cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic pencil or liquid drawn along the lashes is one kind of facial cosmetics.

clue.text: Los Angeles strip is cleaner

parts.note: to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles stripper turns out to be a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose job is to wash and iron clothes and linen is a cleaner of laundry.

clue.text: Deception taking in engineers is very funny thing

indicators.note: one word takes the other into its middle, so the engineers sit inside the deception

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or con
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A fraud that fools even the engineers turns out to be hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something or someone hilarious is called a riot or a hoot, this word being another such term.

clue.text: Secretive about worship, in a way that lacks depth

definitions.text: in a way that lacks depth

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: sly means cunning and secretive
to hallow is to revere as holy

explanation.surface: A furtive person is evasive about religion and lacks depth.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb describes acting superficially, with little depth or seriousness.

clue.text: Name item in pie around Christmas primarily

definitions.text: Name item in pie around Christmas primarily

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters enclose the initial
printer's pie is a jumble of type, so these letters are rearranged
primarily means first, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Something eaten in a pie at Christmas time is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pie' is a printing term for jumbled type: NAME ITEM shuffles to MINEMEAT, and 'around' wraps it about C, the first of Christmas; the whole clue describes the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiced dried-fruit filling baked into small pies at Christmas is this sweet preserve.

clue.text: Group of actors in rep out for a change

indicators.note: changing the words means rearranging their letters here

explanation.surface: A theatre company is pulled out of repertory to try something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' suggests repertory theatre in the surface, but it is just three letters of anagram fodder with OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A company of travelling performers, especially players or dancers, is this kind of band.

clue.text: Regret about detective

parts.note: re means concerning, about
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of novels and TV

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry about a police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret or guilt for a wrong done is a feeling of contrition.

clue.text: One put on guard supports family

parts.note: to bear something is to hold up its weight
kin means relatives

explanation.surface: A sentry on duty is someone who backs up his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One put on guard' reads as a sentry, but it is the tall fur cap that is put on the heads of the Guards regiments outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall black fur cap worn by British Guards soldiers is put on a guardsman's head.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts

definitions.meaning: long yellow tropical fruit, in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a curved yellow fruit, also slang meaning crazy, as in driving someone round the bend.

clue.text: Supreme power to make monk dig furiously

indicators.note: furious action suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frantic monk digs to win ultimate authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal sovereignty or authority, as in 'thine is the kingdom, the power and the glory'.

clue.text: Boy catching gnat gets bit

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it as if it had caught it

parts.note: a son is a male child
a midge is a small biting fly like a gnat

explanation.surface: A lad who catches an insect ends up getting bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the past tense of bite in the surface, fitting the gnat, but it is the noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity, a little piece, is a variant spelling of the informal word for a very small amount.

clue.text: Michael Finnegan's content being small

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters are inside the words

explanation.surface: Michael Finnegan of the nursery rhyme is small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy, but read as the noun it means what the name holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a fairy or sprite, diminutive and delicate in build.

clue.text: Make sudden move forward pinching old saloon

indicators.note: pinching is gripping between two parts, so one word encloses the letter for old

parts.note: to lunge is to thrust suddenly forward

explanation.surface: A thief darts forward to steal a vintage car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' suggests a car with 'pinching' as theft, but it means a comfortable room of a pub or hotel, the British saloon bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs, the more comfortable bar room is called either the saloon bar or this word bar.

clue.text: Eden Hazard? Golden feet work deftly with energy

indicators.note: deftly working the feet suggests nimble rearrangement of these letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A footballer named Eden Hazard shows dazzling skill with his golden feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden Hazard is a Belgian footballer, which fits the golden feet; the definition reads it as a danger in the Garden of Eden, the tree whose fruit Adam and Eve were forbidden to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the forbidden tree in the Garden of Eden was a peril, since eating its fruit led to the Fall.

clue.text: Place serving officers Horlicks

definitions.meaning: the room where military officers eat together
British slang for a muddle or botched job, from the malted drink brand

explanation.definitionFit: The officers' dining room in a barracks is so called, and in British slang a botch-up is a Horlicks or a shambles.

clue.text: North American animal shed is unpleasant

parts.note: a sty is a pen or shed for pigs

explanation.surface: An American pigpen is a horrid place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disagreeable, horrid or offensive is described with this common adjective.

clue.text: Blue stuff upset stomachs

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tums is informal for stomachs or bellies

explanation.surface: Some blue substance has given people sore bellies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour, but it means indecent, as in a blue joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or obscene material is called blue, and this word means smutty talk or pictures.
